questions.question: In a saltwater solution, what is the dissolved salt called?
choices: Solvent
Suspension
Solute
Precipitate

questions.question: What is the solvent in a solution made by dissolving sugar in water?
choices: Sugar
Both equally
Water
Neither substance

questions.question: Which description defines a solution?
choices: A mixture uniform at the particle level
A mixture with visibly separate layers
A pure compound with a fixed formula
A substance containing only one element

questions.question: What does solubility describe?
choices: The amount of solute added regardless of whether it dissolves
The time taken for a fixed mass to dissolve
The mass of solution left after every solvent evaporates
The maximum amount that can dissolve under specified conditions

questions.question: What is a saturated solution at a given temperature?
choices: A solution with equal masses of solute and solvent
A solution holding its equilibrium maximum of dissolved solute
A solution that can still dissolve more of the same solute
A solution in which no solute particles remain dissolved

questions.question: Which unit can express mass concentration?
choices: Grams of solute per liter of solution
Liters of solvent per second
Meters of solute per gram
Degrees per liter of solvent

questions.question: What is an unsaturated solution?
choices: One containing more solute than its equilibrium limit
One containing no solvent
One that can dissolve additional solute under the same conditions
One that cannot conduct electricity

questions.question: Why does stirring often help sugar dissolve faster?
choices: It makes the solvent hotter in every case
It brings fresh solvent into contact with the sugar
It increases the equilibrium solubility at unchanged temperature
It reduces the mass of solute added

questions.question: Why can crushing a solid speed up its dissolving?
choices: Its equilibrium solubility necessarily increases
Its total mass becomes greater
Its solvent concentration decreases before contact
More surface is exposed to the solvent

questions.question: How does adding more solvent usually affect concentration if solute mass stays fixed?
choices: Concentration increases
Solute mass doubles
The solute becomes a pure substance
Concentration decreases

questions.question: Why should solubility data include temperature?
choices: Temperature influences dissolving speed but never solubility
Solubility can change with temperature
Every solute becomes equally soluble at one temperature
Solubility depends only on the amount of stirring

questions.question: How does warming water generally affect the solubility of gases in it?
choices: More gas always remains dissolved at equilibrium
The dissolved amount stays constant regardless of temperature
Less gas can remain dissolved at equilibrium
Gas solubility changes only with container size

questions.question: Why does opening a carbonated drink allow gas to escape?
choices: Lower gas pressure above the liquid reduces dissolved gas solubility
The gas pressure above the liquid increases
The dissolved gas becomes more soluble at lower pressure
Opening changes only the liquid's color, with no gas effect

questions.question: What distinguishes dissolving rate from solubility?
choices: Rate describes mass; solubility describes color
Rate describes speed; solubility describes an equilibrium limit
Both always describe the same quantity
Solubility measures only the size of particles

questions.question: Why does a clear liquid not necessarily indicate a pure substance?
choices: Dissolved substances may be invisible
Every dissolved substance must change a liquid's color
A solution's clarity shows that it contains only solvent
Dissolved substances always form visible layers

questions.question: A solution contains 10 g of solute in 2 L of solution. What is its mass concentration?
choices: 20 g/L
12 g/L
5 g/L

questions.question: At a certain temperature, 30 g of salt can dissolve in 100 g of water. What happens when 40 g is added and equilibrium is reached?
choices: All 40 g dissolves
Exactly 30 g remains undissolved
All 40 g remains undissolved
About 10 g remains undissolved

questions.question: A solubility graph shows 20 g per 100 g water at 20°C and 40 g at 60°C. What does it support?
choices: All solids follow the same temperature trend
This solute is more soluble at 60°C
The solute necessarily dissolves twice as fast at 60°C
Solubility is independent of temperature

questions.question: A student stirs two identical saturated solutions at the same temperature. Does faster stirring increase the equilibrium amount dissolved?
choices: Yes, faster stirring always doubles the equilibrium solubility
Yes, any stirring prevents saturation
No, because stirring stops dissolved particles from moving
No, stirring mainly changes how quickly equilibrium is reached

questions.question: A solution is diluted from 1 L to 2 L without losing solute. How does its concentration change?
choices: It becomes half the original concentration
It becomes twice the original concentration
It stays unchanged
It becomes four times the original concentration
